findings.title: Split reviews discard usage from all but the first part
findings.description: Each split review part is stamped with its own usage record in `review.py`, but `_metadata` copies only the first part’s metadata. Since pipeline review artifacts are excluded from `sq stats reviews`, the run report then omits the spend from every later part. Preserve or aggregate the per-part records so the run total reflects all calls.

findings.title: Compact paths do not consistently record usage
findings.description: The prompt-only path sends an SDK query but does not capture or stamp its usage, even though `COMPACT` is counted as an LLM action by `sq stats run`. The SDK-rotate path also returns a failed result without usage metadata when an exception carries telemetry. These compact calls can therefore spend tokens while appearing unrecorded.

findings.title: Standalone review stats cannot identify the selected alias
findings.description: The reviews report derives an alias only from `requestedModel`, but review artifacts include that field only for substituted models—and it records the resolved model ID, not the alias. Consequently, standalone reviews normally lose the alias’s `cost_tier`; `stats reviews` can label a subscription provider cost as ordinary `prov` instead of `api-rate equiv.`. Persist the alias separately or otherwise retain it in the artifact.

findings.title: Malformed cost-basis YAML can crash the reviews report
findings.description: `_basis` tests the parsed frontmatter value for membership in a set. If malformed YAML supplies a list or mapping for `costBasis`, this raises `TypeError` because those values are unhashable, aborting the report instead of warning and treating the field as unknown. Validate that the value is a string before the membership check.
